task.title: Add AI-generated subject lines to queue messages
task.description: Update the AI message generation to also produce a subject line. (1) In generateMsg(), change the JSON return format in the prompt from {reason:...,message:...} to {reason:...,subject:...,message:...}. The subject should be 5-8 words, human and specific, no 'Following up' cliches unless genuinely appropriate. (2) After parsing the response, store parsed.subject in a variable. (3) When adding to queue via addToQueue(), include subject:parsed.subject||'' in the queue item object. (4) When adding to drafts via saveDraft(), include subject:parsed.subject||'' in the draft item. (5) In renderQueue(), display the subject above the message preview: add a div showing the subject in 13px italic gray text if item.subject exists. (6) In sendEmail(qid), use item.subject if it exists, otherwise fall back to the current generated string. (7) In bulkSendAll(), same — use item.subject if available. (8) In refineDraft() and refineQueueMsg(), after rewriting the message, make a second small API call to regenerate the subject: call claude-haiku with prompt 'Given this email body, write a subject line (5-8 words, no cliches): [message]' and update the subject field.
task.project_vision: Frontend-only AI outreach SaaS. Single HTML file. localStorage. Surgical edits only.

issues: Minor: The subject line input in queue items uses `onchange` instead of `input` event, which means changes only register when focus is lost. This works but is slightly less responsive than the drafts version which doesn't have this issue.
data.feedback:
The implementation successfully adds AI-generated subject lines to queue messages. The code correctly:

1. **Generates subject lines** via the Claude API in `generateMsg()` - returns `{subject, reason, message}` JSON
2. **Stores subject in queue items** - each queue entry has a `subject` field that persists
3. **Displays subject in queue UI** - shows an editable subject field in the queue list
4. **Provides fallback** - `defaultSubject()` generates a subject if AI doesn't provide one or for legacy items
5. **Allows editing** - `updateQSubject()` lets users modify the subject before sending
6. **Uses subject in compose** - `sendEmail()` passes the queue item's subject to email compose
7. **Maintains in drafts** - subject is preserved when converting queue items to drafts

The JSON parsing is robust with the `parseJsonLoose()` function handling malformed AI responses. The subject line requirement (3-7 words, specific reason, no emojis) is correctly specified in the prompt to Claude.

Minor suggestion: Consider changing the queue subject field from `onchange` to `input` event for real-time updates, matching the UX pattern elsewhere in the app.

blocking_issues: Truncated code at end - `const sub=(docume` in openGmail() function will cause runtime error when user clicks 'Open in Gmail' button
Close button 'x' has no accessible label (aria-label) for screen readers
Input field lacks associated label element for accessibility
No keyboard focus trap management in modal - users can tab to elements behind the guide overlay
Modal overlay missing role='dialog' and aria-modal='true' for screen reader context
Close button and send button lack focus visible states for keyboard navigation
No focus trap in modals - keyboard users can tab outside modal overlay to underlying content, breaking accessibility
No keyboard accessibility for closing modals - ESC key handler missing, users dependent on keyboard cannot dismiss modals
Logout button has no confirmation - clicking sidebar logout immediately logs user out with no warning or undo option
No loading states on data submission - forms/buttons provide no feedback during async operations, users may double-submit
Search and filter inputs have no aria-labels - screen readers cannot identify purpose of these controls
Code truncation at line end: `const sub=(docume` in openGmail() function will cause runtime error - critical syntax error that breaks Gmail compose functionality
Close button 'x' has insufficient touch target size (2px padding = ~24px min) - must be at least 44x44px for mobile accessibility (WCAG 2.5.5)
No keyboard focus indicators visible on interactive elements (input, buttons) - fails WCAG 2.4.7
